newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Toatsu's first half profits rise 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Toatsu's first half profits rise 20 pct.

text.p: Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc, which will merge with another firm next year to become Japan's second biggest chemical company, managed to increase its profit for the first half of the business year by 20 percent despite a tough business environment.

"The business situation in the chemical industry was difficult as product prices fell at home and abroad and naphtha prices increased. But our profits rose because of robust sales of electronics-related products," a company spokesman said on Thursday after the results were announced.

Mitsui Toatsu, which is a member of the Mitsui conglomerate, posted a parent current profit of 4.18 billion yen ($37.6 million) in the six months to September 30, 1996, up 20.4 percent from the same period a year ago. Its half-year sales were 191.64 billion yen ($1.72 billion), virtually unchanged from a year earlier.
Current profit is pre-tax but includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.

While sales of plastics, basic chemicals and chemical products dropped, sales of electronics-related products rose sharply due to heavy demand from the electronics and telecommunications industries, he said.

Mitsui Toatsu expects its parent current profits to grow to 13 billion yen ($117 million) in the full business year to March 31, 1997, compared with 11.31 billion yen ($101 million) in the previous year.

Mitsui Toatsu announced last month that it would merge with Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd, a chemical maker in the Mitsui group, on October 1, 1997, to boost its competitiveness in the global chemical market.
Mitsui Toatsu will be dissolved upon the merger.
The new company, to be called Mitsui Chemicals Inc, will become the second-largest chemical producer in Japan after Mitsubishi Chemical Corp which was also created through a merger in 1994.
Mitsui Petrochemical announced last month that its April-September current profit slipped 10 percent year-on-year to 7.65 billion yen ($68.9 million). ($1=111 yen)
